answer.location_description: Small square patch in the top-left corner of the image, about rows 1-3 and columns 1-3, well away from the central blob.
answer.mechanism: There are two groups of first-layer units. The first group (0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 18, 20, 29) responds to large blobs and also has strong positive weights (about +40 to +99) on the 3x3 top-left patch. The second group (5, 6, 9, 14, 15, 21, 24, 27, 30) responds to small blobs or background and has strong negative weights (about -40 to -98) on the same patch. A bright patch therefore switches on the large-blob units and suppresses the small-blob units. In layer 2, the first group feeds the layer-2 units that push the output up (u3, u10, u12, u13: e.g. u10 takes +87, +94, +91, +89 from units 0, 1, 8, 18; u3 takes +84 to +94 from units 2, 4, 8, 10). The second group feeds the layer-2 units that push the output down (u0, u1, u6: e.g. u0 takes +84 and +93 from units 9 and 21; u6 takes +87, +78, +71 from units 5, 21, 27). The net effect of a bright patch is a higher logit, i.e. a push toward class 1 (large blob).
answer.evidence: The weights in rows 1-3, columns 1-3 are by far the largest-magnitude weights in about 18 of the 32 first-layer units. Examples: unit 4 has 93, 98, 98, 94; unit 20 has 81-94; unit 5 has -82 to -98; unit 14 has -77, -98, -82. Neighbouring pixels such as row 0 and column 0 or 4 carry only small weights of mixed sign. The sign of the patch weight in each unit matches that unit's blob-size preference: units that are positive on a broad ring at rows 5-17 and columns 5-18 are also positive on the patch. The six units with no structured weights (3, 7, 11, 12, 13, 16, 17, 19, 22, 23, 25, 26, 28, 31 among others) look like noise and have no patch structure.
answer.main_feature: The model compares how much brightness lies in a wide central disk or annulus (roughly rows 5-18, columns 5-18) with the surrounding background. Large blobs light up the outer ring that large-blob units weight positively; small blobs leave that ring dark, which activates units that weight the ring negatively and the periphery positively.
